concepts.name: NICo (NVIDIA Infra Controller)
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's platform for managing the full lifecycle of bare-metal servers at a site, with tenant isolation enforced by DPUs. It has two halves: NICo Core, the on-site control plane, and NICo REST, the cloud-facing API.

concepts.name: NICo Core
concepts.definition: The on-site Rust control plane of NICo. It runs as microservices (API, DHCP, DNS, hardware monitoring, rack management) on a Kubernetes cluster and exposes a gRPC API.

concepts.name: NICo REST
concepts.definition: The cloud-facing Go API layer of NICo. It handles external HTTP requests, authenticates callers with JWTs, and sends site work to Core through Temporal workflows and a Site Agent.

concepts.name: ManagedHost
concepts.definition: The basic unit NICo manages: one physical box made up of a Host machine and the DPU machines attached to it (usually one, sometimes several or none).

concepts.name: Instance
concepts.definition: A Host that is currently allocated to a tenant. It comes with validated hardware, isolated networking, and DHCP/DNS service.

concepts.name: Data Processing Unit (DPU)
concepts.definition: A smart network card with its own Arm CPU, OS and BMC. In NICo it is the main enforcement point: it acts as the VXLAN tunnel endpoint, runs HBN, and enforces tenant isolation in hardware.

concepts.name: BlueField
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's family of DPU and SuperNIC products. BlueField models that can run as DPUs have an Arm complex, a BMC, NIC firmware and an OS image that NICo provisions.

concepts.name: SuperNIC
concepts.definition: A high-performance NVIDIA/Mellanox network card, such as BlueField-3 in NIC mode or a ConnectX-8. A NIC-only SuperNIC cannot switch into DPU mode.

concepts.name: Host DPU Policy
concepts.definition: The operator's chosen treatment of DPU hardware on a host. `Manage` lets NICo provision the DPUs, `Nic` runs them as plain NICs, and `Ignore` leaves them unconfigured. It records intent, not what the hardware is actually doing.

concepts.name: BlueField Operating Mode
concepts.definition: The mode (`Dpu` or `Nic`) that a BlueField card's own BMC reports it is running in. NICo compares it with the Host DPU Policy to decide whether the card needs reconfiguring.

concepts.name: Mellanox Device Kind
concepts.definition: The factory product class NICo derives from a card's part number. It identifies the SKU and does not change when the card's operating mode changes.

concepts.name: Zero-DPU Host
concepts.definition: A managed host that runs without a NICo-managed DPU, because its policy is `ignore` or `nic`. NICo builds no overlay for it; its instances attach to HostInband segments inside Flat VPCs.

concepts.name: Baseboard Management Controller (BMC)
concepts.definition: A small controller on a machine that manages low-level hardware functions such as power and BIOS settings, independently of the main OS. Hosts and DPUs each have their own BMC.

concepts.name: Redfish API
concepts.definition: The standard HTTP API that BMCs expose for out-of-band hardware management. NICo uses it for power control, credentials and other BMC operations.

concepts.name: Out-of-Band Management (OOB)
concepts.definition: Managing a machine through a path that does not depend on its OS, usually a dedicated BMC/DPU management network. IPMI is an older protocol for this.

concepts.name: BMC Discovery
concepts.definition: How NICo finds BMCs. A BMC requests an IP address over DHCP (relayed to NICo), and NICo matches its MAC address against the expected-machines table to look up its initial credentials.

concepts.name: DHCP
concepts.definition: The protocol that automatically assigns IP addresses to devices. NICo runs its own DHCP service, and switches must relay DHCP requests from BMC and DPU management networks to it.

concepts.name: DNS
concepts.definition: The system that turns names into IP addresses. NICo runs DNS for its managed machines and control-plane zones.

concepts.name: PXE and iPXE Boot
concepts.definition: Ways to boot a machine from software fetched over the network. NICo runs a PXE server that installs its own images and tenant-requested images on DPUs and Hosts.

concepts.name: BFB (BlueField Bootstream)
concepts.definition: The image format used to install or update the OS and firmware bundle on a BlueField DPU.

concepts.name: Cloud-init
concepts.definition: The standard tool that configures an OS on first boot (networking, SSH keys, packages). NICo uses it to install its components on DPUs, and tenants can supply their own for Hosts.

concepts.name: Managed Host State Machine
concepts.definition: The finite state machine that drives a Host through its lifecycle: DPU discovery, DPU/host init, BOM validation, validation, measurement, Ready, Assigned. It also has reprovisioning and failure states.

concepts.name: Finite State Machine
concepts.definition: A model in which an object is always in exactly one of a fixed set of states and moves between them according to defined transitions. NICo's controllers use these to drive hosts and racks.

concepts.name: State Controller Tick
concepts.definition: The periodic loop in which a state handler reloads an object from the database, checks its config flags, and performs any transition. A gRPC call only sets a flag; the actual transition happens on a later tick.

concepts.name: Host Reprovision
concepts.definition: The managed-host substates that upgrade a host's firmware, including the failure state FailedFirmwareUpgrade. Retries there are automatic and bounded, but a fresh reprovision request restarts the upgrade straight away.

concepts.name: SKU / BOM Validation
concepts.definition: Checking that a machine's actual hardware (its bill of materials) matches the expected SKU before it can reach Ready.

concepts.name: Rack State Machine
concepts.definition: The state machine that manages a whole rack (compute trays, switches, power shelves) through states such as Discovering, Maintenance, Validating, Ready and Error.

concepts.name: Compute Tray
concepts.definition: A compute server module that sits in a rack and appears in NICo as a machine.

concepts.name: Power Shelf
concepts.definition: A rack component that supplies power to the rack's devices. It is handled directly by the component manager rather than by the rack state machine.

concepts.name: On-Demand Rack Maintenance
concepts.definition: A gRPC operation that sets a maintenance request on a rack in Ready or Error. The rack state machine then picks it up, runs the selected maintenance activities, and returns the rack through Validating to Ready.

concepts.name: Maintenance Scope
concepts.definition: The optional lists of machine, switch and power-shelf IDs to maintain. If all three lists are empty, the whole rack is maintained.

concepts.name: Maintenance Activities
concepts.definition: The steps a maintenance run can include: firmware upgrade, NVOS update, power sequence and NMX cluster configuration. They always run in that fixed order. An empty list selects everything except the power sequence.

concepts.name: Rack Management Service (RMS)
concepts.definition: The rack-level backend service that NICo calls to perform firmware upgrades and switch system-image updates.

concepts.name: SOT JSON
concepts.definition: A JSON document that defines the target firmware or system-image configuration and is passed to RMS. It comes either from the rack profile's firmware object or from an explicit maintenance activity.

concepts.name: NVOS
concepts.definition: The NVIDIA operating system that runs on rack switches. It is updated through RMS's ApplySwitchSystemImage call.

concepts.name: Component Manager
concepts.definition: A higher-level firmware-update API. For compute trays and switches it hands the work to on-demand rack maintenance; it updates power shelves itself.

concepts.name: gRPC
concepts.definition: An RPC framework that uses protobuf-defined services. It is the API style of NICo Core, used by the CLI and the Site Agent.

concepts.name: Protocol Buffers (protobuf)
concepts.definition: Google's language for defining interfaces and serializing data. A `oneof` field holds exactly one of several variants; NICo uses it to represent the type of each maintenance activity.

concepts.name: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
concepts.definition: Granting permissions to roles instead of individual users. For example, Core grants OnDemandRackMaintenance to the NicoAdminCLI role, and REST uses provider/tenant admin and viewer roles.

concepts.name: NMX-C
concepts.definition: The controller that manages NVLink partitions so that tenants are isolated GPU-to-GPU. Rack maintenance can configure its cluster.

concepts.name: NVLink
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's high-speed GPU-to-GPU interconnect fabric. It is partitioned by NMX-C, outside NICo Core.

concepts.name: SuperNIC Lockdown
concepts.definition: A card mode that blocks firmware and configuration changes unless the card is unlocked with a 64-bit key, so host tenants cannot tamper with the NIC. Losing the key effectively bricks the card.

concepts.name: ASTRA
concepts.definition: An NVIDIA hardware architecture (e.g. ConnectX-9 with BF4) in which SuperNICs are locked by design and managed only through the DPU, so NICo does no key management.

concepts.name: S-VPC
concepts.definition: A non-ASTRA deployment flavour (for example on BF3) where SuperNICs are flashed so that NICo must manage their lockdown keys.

concepts.name: Key Derivation Function (KDF)
concepts.definition: A function that deterministically produces cryptographic keys from secret input material plus context. The same inputs always give the same key, and different contexts give independent keys.

concepts.name: HKDF-SHA256
concepts.definition: The standard HMAC-based KDF from RFC 5869. NICo applies it with no salt and an info string of `supernic-lock:v1:{mac}:{machine_id}` to produce each card's 8-byte lockdown key.

concepts.name: Input Key Material (IKM)
concepts.definition: The secret, high-entropy, site-wide value that all lockdown keys are derived from. It is versioned and kept in the credential store, and the key cannot be re-derived without the exact version used.

concepts.name: KDF Context
concepts.definition: The non-secret inputs that tie a derived key to one card: its MAC address and the owning host's MachineId, encoded in the versioned V1 format.

concepts.name: MachineId
concepts.definition: NICo's stable identifier for a machine (Host or DPU). It is used as an input when deriving keys.

concepts.name: Entropy and Offline Guessing
concepts.definition: A secret's strength comes from how unpredictable it is. HKDF adds no entropy, so if a card key leaks, a weak IKM could be guessed offline.

concepts.name: Lockdown IKM Rotation
concepts.definition: Creating a new IKM version and moving cards to it. Cards migrate at allocation or through idle unlock/re-lock, and the version chosen depends on in-flight, current and site-target bookkeeping.

concepts.name: DPA Interface
concepts.definition: NICo's record and lifecycle for a SuperNIC attached to a host. It moves through Unlocking, firmware/profile application, Locking and Assigned.

concepts.name: Scout
concepts.definition: A NICo agent that reports discovered hardware to Core and runs hardware operations such as SuperNIC lock and unlock.

concepts.name: dpu-agent
concepts.definition: A daemon on each provisioned DPU that regularly calls Core's gRPC API to fetch configuration and report state.

concepts.name: Credential Store
concepts.definition: The backend (Vault or Postgres) that holds NICo secrets such as BMC credentials and lockdown IKMs. The Postgres backend encrypts them with key encryption keys.

concepts.name: Key Encryption Key (KEK)
concepts.definition: A key used to encrypt other stored secrets. Every KEK must be kept, or the credential journal cannot be decrypted.

concepts.name: BMC Site-Wide Root Credential
concepts.definition: The site-wide BMC root secret. It is copied once to seed lockdown IKM version 0 and stays independent afterwards.

concepts.name: NIC Firmware Recovery
concepts.definition: A recovery engine, disabled by default, that freezes a card's original lockdown policy, changes its firmware, then restores the original policy and reads it back.

concepts.name: MAC Address
concepts.definition: A network interface's hardware address. NICo uses it to identify cards and BMCs and as a key-derivation input.

concepts.name: VXLAN
concepts.definition: An overlay technology that wraps Ethernet frames in IP/UDP packets tagged with a VNI. Many isolated tenant L2 networks can then share one routed datacenter fabric.

concepts.name: VNI
concepts.definition: The 24-bit ID in a VXLAN header that says which virtual network a packet belongs to.

concepts.name: VTEP
concepts.definition: The device that wraps and unwraps VXLAN packets. In NICo this is the DPU.

concepts.name: VLAN
concepts.definition: A 12-bit tag on an Ethernet frame that marks which virtual network it belongs to. It allows only 4096 IDs, which is too few for large multi-tenant sites.

concepts.name: BGP
concepts.definition: The standard routing protocol for exchanging reachability information. In NICo, DPUs and switches use it to carry EVPN routes.

concepts.name: EVPN
concepts.definition: A BGP-based control plane that tells VTEPs which tenant addresses are reachable where in a VXLAN overlay.

concepts.name: VRF
concepts.definition: Separate routing tables on one device, which keep each tenant's routes isolated.

concepts.name: HBN (Host Based Networking)
concepts.definition: A container on the DPU that runs Cumulus Linux routing components (FRR, NVUE). It handles VXLAN/EVPN and enforces Ethernet tenancy.

concepts.name: VPC
concepts.definition: A tenant's isolated network boundary. NICo builds it as a DPU overlay (ETV, FNN) or as a Flat VPC.

concepts.name: FNN
concepts.definition: The Core networking subsystem that manages VPCs, subnets and VXLAN overlays. It is also the name of an L3 DPU-overlay VPC type that uses per-VPC routing profiles.

concepts.name: Network Segment
concepts.definition: NICo's definition of an IP address pool. Underlay segments carry management traffic; overlay segments are tenant networks built on VXLAN.

concepts.name: HostInband Network Segment
concepts.definition: An underlay segment that a zero-DPU host's NIC attaches to directly. It is the only segment type a Flat VPC accepts.

concepts.name: Flat VPC
concepts.definition: A VPC type for zero-DPU hosts. NICo allocates addresses and keeps records, but the operator's fabric does the routing and enforcement.

concepts.name: InfiniBand Partitioning (P_Key / UFM)
concepts.definition: Tenant isolation on InfiniBand: Core allocates partition keys and UFM manages which hosts are members of each partition.

concepts.name: Multi-Tenancy and Isolation
concepts.definition: NICo's coordinated isolation across four fabrics: Ethernet north-south (VXLAN/EVPN on DPUs), east-west Ethernet (ConnectX firmware paths where configured), InfiniBand (UFM) and NVLink (NMX-C).

concepts.name: Temporal
concepts.definition: A workflow orchestration engine that NICo REST uses for long-running operations, with one namespace per site.

concepts.name: Site Agent
concepts.definition: An on-site agent that polls the site's Temporal namespace, turns workflow tasks into gRPC calls to Core, and publishes inventory back.

concepts.name: JWT Authentication
concepts.definition: How NICo REST authenticates callers. A JSON Web Token comes from an issuer such as Keycloak, NGC KAS or a service account, and processors map its claims to authorization context.

concepts.name: SPIFFE Identity
concepts.definition: A standard for workload identity. NICo uses it between services, and its DPU metadata service can issue SPIFFE JWT-SVIDs to tenant workloads.

concepts.name: Kubernetes and Helm
concepts.definition: The container orchestration platform that NICo Core and REST run on, and the Helm charts used to deploy them.

concepts.name: DOCA
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's software framework and release train for BlueField DPU functionality.

concepts.name: LLDP
concepts.definition: A neighbour-discovery protocol. NICo uses the adjacency data it provides to learn how hosts, DPUs and switches are cabled together.
